frozen_item_affected: F5 — Probe protocol: observation-harness / subject semantics
contradiction_discovered: RFC §9 listed 'probe timeout' among observation-harness failures that MUST produce UNRUNNABLE. Read literally, a subject that hangs becomes UNRUNNABLE -> ENVIRONMENT: the subject's behaviour is charged to the environment budget and never to DEVELOPER, which is exactly what the harness/subject split exists to prevent. A timeout of the observation harness and a deadline reached by the subject are different facts; the frozen wording did not distinguish them.

discovered_in.implementation: aisef2/probe/python_callable.py: subprocess.TimeoutExpired -> HARNESS_FAILED -> UNRUNNABLE, for a hang before or after the subject was touched

concrete_reproducer: the harness launches, prints READY and dispatches the subject
the old probe: TimeoutExpired -> HARNESS_FAILED -> UNRUNNABLE -> PROBE_UNRUNNABLE, owner ENVIRONMENT, retryable
correct: EXECUTED; the observable 'returns 3 within the window' was not observed -> REFUTED -> UNSATISFIED; at the candidate DEVELOPER
why_implementation_cannot_conform: An implementation that maps a subject hang to anything but UNRUNNABLE contradicts the frozen §9 bullet ('probe timeout MUST produce UNRUNNABLE'); one that follows it charges product behaviour to ENVIRONMENT. Neither conforms to the harness/subject split F5 freezes.

replacement.summary: Freeze the distinction. Harness failure or harness timeout (the observation mechanism cannot operate or cannot obtain an observation) -> UNRUNNABLE / ENVIRONMENT, no verdict. Subject observation deadline (the harness dispatched and observed the subject, which did not complete or emit the expected observation within the spec's bounded window) -> EXECUTED, with the verdict the spec's observable assigns to an expired window. No global 'subject timeout -> REFUTED' and no 'subject timeout -> UNRUNNABLE'; a spec that cannot give its bounded window a meaning is INVALID_SPEC, rejected as early as possible (StaticPlanAdmission).

semantics.subject dispatched, the spec's observati: EXECUTED; the verdict the spec's observable assigns to an expired window
semantics.spec whose observable cannot assign sema: INVALID_SPEC; rejected at StaticPlanAdmission (check 9) and by the probe

replacement.rfc_text: §9 harness-failure bullets, new §9.2, freeze-table F5 row and marker sentence, adversarial cases TIME-1..5, status header

evidence_compatibility_impact.what_changes: The outcome of a subject that exceeds its window: UNRUNNABLE/ENVIRONMENT -> EXECUTED with the observable's verdict. python_callable specs now declare their window (observable 'within_s'); the reference probe's digest changes, so every spec bound to the old digest is refused (INVALID_SPEC, scenario D) and must be recompiled. rfc_normative_digest, freeze_table_digest and the F5 row digest change.
evidence_compatibility_impact.evidence_written_under_the_old_wording: No V2 journal exists (P3). The P2 evidence records at 7c7f7dd (P2-PROBE-PROTOCOL.json fault_injection 'probe timeout' -> UNRUNNABLE) are historical; P2-COMPLETION.json stays byte-identical and is superseded by P2-COMPLETION-CORRECTION-V2-002.json. V1 evidence is untouched.
evidence_compatibility_impact.unaffected: ProbeExecutionStatus x BehaviorVerdict (F2), the Owner set (F3), the Probe protocol members and signatures, ProbeResult fields, the calibration contracts, subject-absence semantics (§10.2)
